chunks.heading: The GitHub Action
chunks.text:
Our [Action for GitHub workflows](https://github.com/jorgeortega/latitude10-action) scores your document in the workflow, can fail the job on a low score or a breaking change, and can push the version to the registry. It's public, under MIT.

## 1. Add the key

Add your project key to the repository's secrets as `LATITUDE10_KEY`. The Action scores and gates without it; pushing and fixes need it.

## 2. Add the step

```yaml
- uses: jorgeortega/latitude10-action@v1
  with:
    spec: openapi.yaml
    min-score: 70          # fail below this; default: report only
    max-tools: 40          # fail above this many operations; default 40
    fail-on-breaking: true # default false
    push: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
    suggest-fixes: true    # any plan; opens or updates one PR
  env:
    LATITUDE10_KEY: ${{ secrets.LATITUDE10_KEY }}   # optional
```

## Inputs

| Input | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spec` | The path to your OpenAPI document, YAML or JSON. Local `$ref`s are bundled. Required. | None |
| `min-score` | Fail when the readiness score is below this, from 0 to 100. | Empty: report only |
| `max-tools` | Fail when the document has more operations than this, since each one becomes an agent tool. | `40` |
| `fail-on-breaking` | Fail when the document has breaking changes against its base. | `false` |
| `push` | With `LATITUDE10_KEY`, push this version to the registry. | `false` |
| `suggest-fixes` | With `LATITUDE10_KEY` on a paid plan, open or update one pull request with rules-only fixes. | `false` |
| `label` | The version's label in the registry. | Empty: `info.version` |
| `github-token` | The token for the fixes pull request. It needs contents and pull-requests write. | The workflow's token |
| `api-url` | The Latitude 10 API. | `https://latitude10.tech` |

## Outputs

| Output | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `score` | The readiness score, from 0 to 100. |
| `operations` | The number of operations. |
| `breaking` | The breaking changes against the base. |
| `version-url` | With `push`, the version's page in the registry. |

The Action has no input for docs yet. Push a docs folder with `curl` from a step of its own.

## Without the Action

One `curl` step pushes the document on every merge to `main`:

```yaml
- name: Push the spec to Latitude 10
  if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
  run: >
    curl --fail-with-body -X POST
    "https://latitude10.tech/api/registry/v1/versions?git_sha=$GITHUB_SHA&git_ref=$GITHUB_REF"
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $LATITUDE10_KEY"
    --data-binary @openapi.yaml
  env:
    LATITUDE10_KEY: ${{ secrets.LATITUDE10_KEY }}
```

[Push a version](push) lists what it answers.

## Where this comes from

- `app/registry/_lib/ci.ts`
- `app/api/registry/v1/versions/route.ts`
- `app/registry/_lib/versions.ts`
- `app/registry/_lib/bundle.ts`
- `app/registry/_lib/usage.ts`

chunks.title: Registry
chunks.heading: Registry
chunks.text:
The registry is where your OpenAPI document lives. Each push from your CI, or an upload on the project's page, becomes a version.

## A version

A version is one copy of your document, numbered `seq` in push order, with an optional label and the Git commit it came from. The registry keeps the document exactly as you sent it, so you can download the original of any version it keeps.

## Its score

Each version is scored from 0 to 100 by the [readiness rules](readiness-rules): how well an AI agent will understand and call your API. The version's report lists every finding and how to fix it.

## Its diff

Each version is compared with the one before it. The diff marks each change [breaking, warning or information](breaking-changes), and the version records how many breaking changes and warnings it has.

## In this section

- [Push a version](push): the request, its parameters and its errors.
- [The GitHub Action](github-action): score, gate and push from a workflow.
- [Readiness rules](readiness-rules): what the score is made of.
- [Breaking changes](breaking-changes): every kind of change the diff finds.
- [Fixes](fixes): rules-only changes that raise the score, as JSON Patch.
- [Versions](versions): how many are kept, and how to read them.

## Where this comes from

- `app/registry/_lib/versions.ts`
- `app/registry/_lib/diff.ts`
- `app/api/readiness/_lib/report.ts`
- `openapi/registry-v1.yaml`

chunks.title: Push a version
chunks.heading: Push a version › 1. Send the document
chunks.text:
`POST /versions` takes the document itself as the request body, YAML or JSON, with a project key:

```sh
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/versions?label=v1.4.0&git_sha=$GITHUB_SHA&git_ref=$GITHUB_REF" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LATITUDE10_KEY" --data-binary @openapi.yaml
```

## 2. Read the answer

A new version answers `201` with its `seq`, `score`, `breaking` and `warnings` counts and `url`, its page in your workspace. If the bytes are the same as the latest version's, you get that version back with `200`, and nothing new is made.

## Parameters

All three are optional query parameters.

| Parameter | What it's for |
| --- | --- |
| `label` | The version's name. Without one, the document's `info.version` is used. |
| `git_sha` | The commit the document came from. |
| `git_ref` | The branch or tag, such as `refs/heads/main`. |

## What the registry accepts

- One OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1 document, in YAML or JSON.
- One file: a `$ref` inside the document works, a `$ref` to another file or a URL is refused. The GitHub Action bundles local files into one before it pushes.
- Up to 2 MB, on every plan.

The registry keeps the newest versions up to your plan's number, and removes the oldest after each push: see [Plans and limits](../get-started/plans-and-limits#registry).

## Errors

| Status | When | The `error` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401` | No project key, or a revoked one. | `Send a project key: Authorization: Bearer l10p_…` |
| `403` | The workspace has more projects than its plan includes. | `This project is read-only: the workspace has more projects than its plan includes.` |
| `409` | Another push landed at the same moment. | `Another version was pushed at the same moment. Push again.` |
| `413` | The body is larger than the registry keeps. | The size sent and the most that's kept. |
| `422` | It isn't OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1, it doesn't parse, or it has an external `$ref`. | What's wrong. For a `$ref`: `External $ref isn't supported here: …` and how to bundle it. |
| `429` | The project's pushes for today are used. | `Quota reached for this period. It resets at …`, with `resetsAt`. |

A push counts against the day's quota before its body is read, so a refused push still counts. Daily quotas reset at midnight UTC.

chunks.title: Readiness rules
chunks.heading: Readiness rules
chunks.text:
Every version you push is scored from 0 to 100 by these rules, version 1.0.4. The version's report lists each rule's findings.

## The score

Each rule applies to some of your operations or parameters, and its share is the part of those that pass. A rule with nothing to apply to passes. The score is the sum of each rule's weight times its share, divided by the total weight (88), times 100, rounded to a whole number.

## The rules

| Rule | What it checks | Weight | How to fix it |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| `operation-ids` | Every operation has a clear operationId | 10 | Give each operation an operationId that says what it does (listOrders, refundOrder). It becomes the tool name. |
| `descriptions` | Descriptions say what the operation does, when to use it, and what it returns | 10 | Write a description of at least 40 characters per operation, different from the others: models pick tools by it. |
| `summaries` | Every operation has a summary | 8 | Add a short summary (under 80 characters): clients show it as the tool's title. |
| `parameter-descriptions` | Parameters are described | 8 | Describe each parameter: its meaning, format and allowed values. |
| `response-schemas` | Success responses have a JSON schema | 8 | Describe what a 2xx response contains with a JSON schema, so agents know what they'll get back. |
| `security` | How to authenticate is described | 8 | Describe your auth in components.securitySchemes and apply it with security. |
| `examples` | Operations have an example | 6 | Add an example for each operation (a parameter, request or response example): models copy examples. |
| `error-responses` | Errors are described | 6 | Document the errors an operation returns (400, 404, 409…) so agents can recover instead of retrying blindly. |
| `pagination` | List endpoints are paginated | 6 | Give list operations a limit and a cursor (or page) parameter: an agent can't read ten thousand rows. |
| `json-bodies` | Request bodies are JSON | 5 | Accept application/json for request bodies agents send (form and multipart bodies can't be tool calls). |
| `idempotency` | Writes have an idempotency story | 5 | Accept an Idempotency-Key header on POST/PATCH (Agentify honours it for agents), so a retry doesn't do the work twice. |
| `enums` | Parameters with a fixed set of values list them | 4 | Give status/sort/type-like parameters an enum (or list the values in the description). |
| `tool-count` | A manageable number of tools, with distinct names | 4 | Keep enabled tools to about 40 per server (models choose worse from long lists), and give operations distinct operationIds. |

## Run them yourself

The same rules are public as [openapi-agent-check](https://www.npmjs.com/package/openapi-agent-check) (MIT), so you can score a document on your machine or in CI before you push it.

To check a spec that's already online without installing anything, paste its URL into the [free check](https://latitude10.tech/agent-readiness/check). It shows the same rules' results and gives you a live badge for your README, scored again at most once a day.

chunks.title: Versions
chunks.heading: Versions › How many are kept
chunks.text:
Each project keeps its newest versions up to your plan's number: see [Plans and limits](../get-started/plans-and-limits#registry). After each push, the oldest beyond that number are deleted, with their source, report and diff.

After a downgrade, the old plan's number still holds for 30 days, so nothing is deleted the day you change plans. After that, the next push trims the list to the new plan's number.

## Reading them

Every call takes your project key.

## 1. List the versions

Newest first:

```sh
curl -sS "$BASE/versions" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LATITUDE10_KEY"
```

## 2. Read one version's report

The score's findings, rule by rule:

```sh
curl -sS "$BASE/versions/3/report" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LATITUDE10_KEY"
```

## 3. Download the original

The document exactly as it was pushed, as YAML or JSON:

```sh
curl -sS "$BASE/versions/3/source" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LATITUDE10_KEY" -o openapi.yaml
```

## 4. Compare any two versions

```sh
curl -sS "$BASE/diff?from=1&to=3" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LATITUDE10_KEY"
```

Each change has a `kind`, a `level` (breaking, warning or info), a JSON `pointer` into the document and a `message`. The kinds are listed in [Breaking changes](breaking-changes).

A version number that isn't a number answers `400`, and one that doesn't exist, or was deleted, answers `404`.

## Where this comes from

- `app/workspace/_lib/quotas.ts`
- `app/registry/_lib/versions.ts`
- `app/api/registry/v1/versions/route.ts`
- `app/api/registry/v1/versions/[seq]/source/route.ts`
- `app/api/registry/v1/versions/[seq]/report/route.ts`
- `app/api/registry/v1/diff/route.ts`
- `app/api/registry/v1/_lib/route.ts`

chunks.title: The SDK config
chunks.heading: The SDK config
chunks.text:
`latitude10.sdk.json` is the body of every generation request, at most 16 KB. An unknown key is a warning; a field that fails its check refuses the request with `422` and a sentence that says what to fix.

```json
{
  "generator": 1,
  "package": "@acme/sdk",
  "clientName": "Acme",
  "firstVersion": "0.1.0",
  "license": { "holder": "Acme, Inc." },
  "homepage": "https://docs.acme.example",
  "exclude": { "operations": ["getInternalStats"] },
  "python": { "package": "acme-sdk", "module": "acme_sdk" }
}
```

## The fields

| Field | What it sets | Checked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `package` | The npm package name. Required. | A valid npm name, scoped or not, in lowercase. |
| `clientName` | The client class's name. | A JavaScript identifier, and not a reserved word. |
| `firstVersion` | The version of the first package. Default `0.1.0`. | A version such as `1.0.0`, with no prerelease. |
| `include` | Only these operations: `{ "tags": […], "operations": […] }`. | Lists of names. |
| `exclude` | Leave these out, in the same shape. | Lists of names. |
| `license` | `{ "holder": "…" }`, the copyright holder in the MIT licence. Default: the workspace. | A name. |
| `repository` | The package's repository link. | An `https://` URL. |
| `homepage` | The package's homepage link. | An `https://` URL. |
| `generator` | The generator's version. | `1`, the only one so far. |
| `python` | The Python package, below. Without it, no Python package can be made. | An object with at least `package`. |

## The python section

| Field | What it sets | Checked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `python.package` | The PyPI project name, normalised as PyPI does. Required. | A valid PyPI name. |
| `python.module` | The import name. Default: the package name with `-` as `_`. | A Python identifier, not a keyword or a standard library module. |
| `python.firstVersion` | The first Python package's version. Default `0.1.0`. | As `firstVersion`. |
| `python.include` | Python's own include filter, in place of the shared one. | As `include`. |
| `python.exclude` | Python's own exclude filter, in place of the shared one. | As `exclude`. |

## One file, two languages

Each language builds from its own view of the file. TypeScript's is the top-level keys. Python's is the same keys with the `python` section's name, module, first version and filters in their place. A package is identified by its own view, so changing a Python key never moves the TypeScript version line, and the reverse.

## Where this comes from

- `app/sdk/_lib/config.ts`
- `app/sdk/_lib/names.ts`
- `app/sdk/_lib/builds.ts`
- `openapi/latitude10.sdk.json`

chunks.title: What the SDKs cover
chunks.heading: What the SDKs cover
chunks.text:
The generator takes OpenAPI 3.0 and 3.1. Swagger 2.0 is refused: convert it first. Whatever it can't turn into code is left out or typed as `unknown`, never guessed, and each case is a line under "Warnings" in the package's `GENERATION.md`.

## Left out

| What | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Webhooks | An SDK only calls the API. |
| Callbacks and response links | The same. |
| Cookie parameters | The SDK doesn't send cookies. |
| A header the SDK sets itself, or one that carries a credential | The client sets it. |
| A header with the same name as a query parameter | They'd be one field. |
| A path that names a parameter nothing declares, or a path parameter that isn't in the path | The method couldn't be built. |
| An API key in a cookie, and security schemes other than API keys, bearer, OAuth 2, OpenID Connect and basic | Not supported. |
| An operation with `x-latitude10-sdk.exclude`, or outside `include` and `exclude` | You asked. |

## Typed as unknown

| What | Note |
| --- | --- |
| A `$ref` to another file or a URL | Only local `$ref`s are read. |
| A `$ref` that doesn't resolve, or a chain of too many | |
| A schema nested too deeply | |
| `not`, and `patternProperties` | They can't be typed. |
| Schemas that refer to each other with no object in between | |
| A document with more schema types than the generator takes | The rest are `unknown`. |

## The operations cap

A document with more operations than the generator takes is refused with `403`, whatever the plan. Below that, a document with more operations than your plan's endpoints is refused too: use `include` or `exclude` to generate fewer. See [Plans and limits](../get-started/plans-and-limits#sdks).

## Where this comes from

- `app/sdk/_lib/model.ts`
- `app/sdk/_lib/builds.ts`
- `app/sdk/_lib/names.ts`
- `tests/fixtures/sdk/`

chunks.title: SDKs
chunks.heading: SDKs
chunks.text:
On Pro and up, your CI asks the registry API for an SDK made from a registry version and your `latitude10.sdk.json`, and gets the package back as a `.tgz`. It then publishes it to your own npm or PyPI account. We never publish for you, and the generated code is yours, under the MIT licence.

- **TypeScript:** an ESM package with no runtime dependencies, for Node.js 20+, Deno, Bun, Workers and browsers.
- **Python:** a package for Python 3.11+, with `httpx` as its one dependency.

Each package's version follows the registry's breaking-change diff, and the same config and registry version give the same package again.

## 1. Add the config

Commit a `latitude10.sdk.json` naming your package: see [The config](config).

## 2. Generate the package

```sh
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/sdks/typescript?version=latest" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LATITUDE10_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @latitude10.sdk.json -o sdk.tgz
```

`version` is `latest`, the default, or a registry version number.

Members can also download a preview of the package from the SDK section of the project's Overview.

How many endpoints an SDK may have, and how many builds a project gets a day, depend on the plan: see [Plans and limits](../get-started/plans-and-limits#sdks).

## In this section

- [The config](config): every field of `latitude10.sdk.json`.
- [The TypeScript package](typescript): its files, retries, errors and pagination.
- [The Python package](python): its clients, types and errors.
- [The publishing workflow](workflow): from a push to npm and PyPI.
- [SDK versioning](versioning): how each version is worked out.
- [OpenAPI extensions](openapi-extensions): naming, grouping and pagination.
- [Coverage](coverage): what's left out or typed as unknown.

## Where this comes from

- `app/sdk/_lib/builds.ts`
- `app/sdk/_lib/config.ts`
- `app/api/registry/v1/sdks/typescript/route.ts`
- `app/sdk/_lib/typescript/emit.ts`

chunks.title: OpenAPI extensions for SDKs
chunks.heading: OpenAPI extensions for SDKs
chunks.text:
The generator reads two extensions on an operation, both ours. Other vendors' `x-` keys aren't read.

## x-latitude10-sdk

`x-latitude10-sdk` names and groups an operation's method:

```yaml
paths:
  /orders:
    get:
      operationId: listOrders
      x-latitude10-sdk:
        name: list
        group: orders
```

| Field | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | The method's name, in place of the operationId. |
| `group` | The resource the method goes in, in place of the operation's first tag. |
| `exclude` | `true` leaves the operation out of the SDK. |

Without it, a method is named from the operationId, or else from its method and path, and grouped by its first tag.

## x-latitude10-pagination

`x-latitude10-pagination` declares how an operation pages, so its method can walk every page:

```yaml
x-latitude10-pagination:
  type: cursor
  cursorParam: cursor
  nextCursor: $.next_cursor
  items: $.data
```

| `type` | Also needs |
| --- | --- |
| `cursor` | `cursorParam`, a query parameter, and `nextCursor`, a path in the response. |
| `offset` | `offsetParam` and `limitParam`, two different query parameters. |
| `page` | `pageParam`, a query parameter. |

Every type needs `items`, the path of the list in the response, such as `$.data`. A declaration that's missing something leaves the operation unpaginated, with a warning in `GENERATION.md` saying what.

## Detected without the extension

Only one common shape is detected, never guessed: a query parameter named `cursor`, `after`, `starting_after` or `page_token`, and a response object with exactly one array property and either a `next_cursor` or `next_page_token` field, or a `has_more` field with items that have an `id`, the last of which is the next cursor.

## Where this comes from

- `app/sdk/_lib/model.ts`
- `app/sdk/_lib/names.ts`
- `tests/fixtures/sdk/`

chunks.title: The Python package
chunks.heading: The Python package
chunks.text:
A package for Python 3.11 or newer, with one dependency, `httpx`. It has a sync and an async client, and type hints throughout.

## Its files

| File | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `pyproject.toml` | The name, version, `requires-python = ">=3.11"`, the `httpx` dependency, and pyright in strict mode. |
| `src/<module>/_client.py` | The sync and async clients. |
| `src/<module>/resources/` | The operations, grouped by tag, a method each. |
| `src/<module>/types.py` | A `TypedDict` for each schema. |
| `src/<module>/_core.py` | The runtime, the same file in every Python SDK we generate. |
| `src/<module>/py.typed` | The marker that tells type checkers the package is typed. |
| `README.md`, `GENERATION.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `LICENSE` | As in the TypeScript package. |

The code is laid out as `ruff format` lays it out, so `ruff format --check` passes, and it type-checks under pyright's strict mode.

## Clients

The client is named from `clientName`, and its async twin has `Async` in front: `Acme` and `AsyncAcme`. Both take the same arguments. Credentials are passed in, never read from the environment. Pass `http_client=` to use your own `httpx.Client`, and close a client with `close()`, `aclose()` for the async one, or a `with` block.

## Retries, errors and responses

- Connection errors, timeouts, `408`, `429` and `5xx` are retried with backoff, and `Retry-After` is honoured. `POST` and `PATCH` are retried only with an idempotency key: `idempotency_key=` on a call, or one made for you when the operation declares an `Idempotency-Key` header. Set `max_retries` and `timeout` on the client or per call.
- A response outside `2xx` raises an `APIError` with `status_code`, `headers`, `body` and `request_id`, as the same classes the TypeScript package throws. A network failure raises `APIConnectionError`, a timeout `APITimeoutError`.
- Methods return the parsed JSON body, typed by the `TypedDict`s. Every method has a `…_with_response` sibling that returns `(data, response)`, the `httpx.Response`.

## Where this comes from

- `app/sdk/_lib/python/emit.ts`
- `app/sdk/_lib/python/types.ts`
- `app/sdk/_lib/python/layout.ts`
- `app/sdk/_lib/python/runtime/_core.py`
- `tests/fixtures/sdk/petstore/expected-python/README.md`

chunks.title: The TypeScript package
chunks.heading: The TypeScript package
chunks.text:
An ESM package with strict types and no runtime dependencies. It uses the standard `fetch`, so it runs on Node.js 20+, Deno, Bun, Cloudflare Workers and in browsers, and it never calls Latitude 10.

## Its files

| File | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `package.json` | The name and version, `"type": "module"` and `"engines": { "node": ">=20" }`. |
| `src/client.ts` | The client class, named by `clientName`. |
| `src/resources/` | The operations, grouped by tag, a method each. |
| `src/models.ts` | The types from your document's schemas. |
| `src/core.ts` | The runtime, the same file in every SDK we generate. It holds no text from your document. |
| `src/index.ts` | What the package exports. |
| `README.md` | Install, use, each resource's methods, errors and retries. |
| `GENERATION.md` | How it was generated, and anything skipped. |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | What changed in each version. |
| `LICENSE` | MIT, in the holder's name. |
| `tsconfig.json` | The build settings. |

## Auth

The client takes `apiKeys` by security scheme name, `bearerToken` as a string or a function it asks before every request, so you can refresh it, or `username` and `password` for basic auth. Each operation sends the first of its schemes the client has credentials for.

## Retries and timeouts

- Connection errors, timeouts, `408`, `429` and `5xx` are retried with backoff, and `Retry-After` is honoured.
- `POST` and `PATCH` are retried only with an idempotency key: `idempotencyKey` in a call's options, or one made for you when the operation declares an `Idempotency-Key` header.
- Set `maxRetries` and `timeoutMs` on the client or per call, and pass `signal` to cancel.

## Errors

A response outside `2xx` throws an `APIError` with `status`, `headers`, `body` and `requestId`, as one of `BadRequestError`, `AuthenticationError`, `PermissionDeniedError`, `NotFoundError`, `ConflictError`, `UnprocessableEntityError`, `RateLimitError` or `InternalServerError`. A network failure throws `APIConnectionError`, a timeout `APITimeoutError`. All of them extend the client's own error class.

Every method also has a `…WithResponse` sibling that returns `{ data, response }`, for the headers and the status.

## Pagination

An operation that pages, by cursor, offset or page number, returns a page you can await for the first page, or walk with `for await` for every item of every page. [OpenAPI extensions](openapi-extensions) says how a paging operation is found, and `GENERATION.md` says which methods page.

## Where this comes from

- `app/sdk/_lib/typescript/emit.ts`
- `app/sdk/_lib/typescript/runtime/core.ts`
- `app/sdk/_lib/model.ts`
- `tests/fixtures/sdk/petstore/expected/README.md`

chunks.title: SDK versioning
chunks.heading: SDK versioning
chunks.text:
The first package of each language gets your config's `firstVersion`. After that, each package's version is worked out from the last one, the registry's diff between their versions, and the names the SDK exports. The biggest bump that applies wins.

| What changed | Bump |
| --- | --- |
| A breaking change in the diff, or a changed operationId (a renamed method) | Major |
| An exported name is gone from the SDK | Major |
| Any other change in the diff, such as a new operation or a deprecation | Minor |
| A new exported name | Minor |
| No diff to compare with | Minor, compared by exported names only |
| Only a removed description, or nothing | Patch |

[Breaking changes](../registry/breaking-changes) lists every kind of change the diff finds.

## Below 1.0.0

As semver does for versions below `1.0.0`, a major change moves the minor number, and anything else the patch: `0.3.2` becomes `0.4.0` or `0.3.3`.

## The same input, the same package

The same config and the same registry version give the same package and version again, so a re-run never moves the version.

## Previews

A preview from the SDK panel is versioned so it can't be mistaken for a release: `0.0.0-preview.7` for TypeScript and `0.0.0.dev7` for Python, for registry version 7. A preview can be made from the sample document; a package to publish can't.

chunks.heading: The publishing workflow
chunks.text:
The SDK section of the project's Overview shows a whole workflow for `.github/workflows/sdk.yml`. On every push to `main` that changes `openapi.yaml` or `latitude10.sdk.json`, it pushes the document to the registry, generates the TypeScript package, builds it and publishes it to npm, then does the same for Python when the config has a `python` section.

## 1. Add the key

Save your project key as the repository secret `LATITUDE10_KEY`.

## 2. Set up trusted publishing

On npm and on PyPI, add this repository and workflow as a trusted publisher for your package. The workflow then publishes with your own accounts' trust: npm with provenance, PyPI through its trusted publishing.

chunks.title: The publishing workflow
chunks.heading: The publishing workflow › 3. Add the workflow
chunks.text:
```yaml
name: SDK
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: [openapi.yaml, latitude10.sdk.json]
permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write # npm trusted publishing
jobs:
  sdk:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
          registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org
      - name: Push the spec to Latitude 10
        run: >
          curl --fail-with-body -X POST
          "https://latitude10.tech/api/registry/v1/versions?git_sha=$GITHUB_SHA&git_ref=$GITHUB_REF"
          -H "Authorization: Bearer $LATITUDE10_KEY"
          --data-binary @openapi.yaml
        env:
          LATITUDE10_KEY: ${{ secrets.LATITUDE10_KEY }}
      - name: Generate the SDK
        run: >
          curl --fail-with-body -X POST
          "https://latitude10.tech/api/registry/v1/sdks/typescript?version=latest"
          -H "Authorization: Bearer $LATITUDE10_KEY"
          -H "Content-Type: application/json"
          --data-binary @latitude10.sdk.json -o sdk.tgz
          && tar -xzf sdk.tgz
        env:
          LATITUDE10_KEY: ${{ secrets.LATITUDE10_KEY }}
      - name: Build the SDK
        working-directory: package
        run: npm install --no-audit --no-fund && npm run build
      - name: Publish it unless this version is already on npm
        working-directory: package
        run: |
          NAME=$(node -p 'require("./package.json").name')
          VERSION=$(node -p 'require("./package.json").version')
          if npm view "$NAME@$VERSION" version > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "$NAME@$VERSION is already on npm"
          else
            npm publish --provenance --access public
          fi
        # Without trusted publishing, save an npm token as NPM_TOKEN and uncomment:
        # env:
        #   NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
  python-sdk:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: sdk
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write # PyPI trusted publishing
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
      - name: Generate the Python SDK
        run: >
          curl --fail-with-body -X POST
          "https://latitude10.tech/api/registry/v1/sdks/python?version=latest"
          -H "Authorization: Bearer $LATITUDE10_KEY"
          -H "Content-Type: application/json"
          --data-binary @latitude10.sdk.json -o sdk-python.tgz
          && mkdir -p sdk-python && tar -xzf sdk-python.tgz -C sdk-python
        env:
          LATITUDE10_KEY: ${{ secrets.LATITUDE10_KEY }}
      - name: Type-check and build the Python SDK
        working-directory: sdk-python/package
        run: python -m pip install build pyright httpx && pyright && python -m build
      - name: Publish it to PyPI unless this version is already there
        uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
        with:
          packages-dir: sdk-python/package/dist
          skip-existing: true
          # Without trusted publishing, save a PyPI API token as PYPI_API_TOKEN and uncomment:
          # password: ${{ secrets.PYPI_API_TOKEN }}
```

chunks.text:
The same facts are on [our security page](https://latitude10.tech/security).

## How it works

- The site, the APIs, hosted references, docs and MCP servers run as one Cloudflare Worker.
- Workspace data is in one Cloudflare D1 database; versions of your OpenAPI document and docs bundles are in one private R2 bucket.
- Hosted references and docs load no third-party script or font, and each response sends its own content security policy. Our own pages report errors to Sentry, with identifiers removed first.
- Your API credential for hosted MCP is sealed with AES-GCM 256 under a Worker secret, with a fresh IV each time, and one module decrypts it.
- CI keys and MCP keys are stored only as SHA-256 hashes, and shown once.
- Anyone can add passkeys or an authenticator app to their account as a second step at sign-in, and a workspace owner can require MFA for everyone in the workspace. Our own admin area takes only a sign-in that used a passkey.
- You can sign out of every device at once from your account page, and we can do it for you if your account is taken over.
- MCP sign-in tokens are bound to one server and never sent to your API.
- The API client’s proxy (Pro) calls only hosts you verified, follows no redirects and stores nothing.
- Fixes to your spec are rules-only JSON Patch: no workspace feature sends your spec to an AI model. The paid readiness report on our public site does, outside the workspace.
- Sign-in is with GitHub or an emailed link that works once, for 15 minutes. SSO is OpenID Connect, on Business and Enterprise.
- The audit log is append-only: the database refuses changes, and deletes of events younger than 30 days. It's kept 90 days on Business and 365 on Enterprise.
- Each project keeps its last 10 versions on Free, 200 on Pro and 1,000 on Business. After a downgrade, the old plan's number holds for 30 days.
- Deleting a project, a workspace or your account deletes it at once; database backups keep it for up to 30 more days.
- The SDK runtime, the agent-readiness rules and the CI Action are public, and request collections export to Postman.
- Uptime is published on our status page, and the SLA covers Enterprise.
- Every response is sent with MIME sniffing off, a strict referrer policy, browser features such as the camera turned off, and no framing by other sites unless a page is meant to be embedded; on our own domains, browsers are also told to use only HTTPS.
- Our tests, which run before every automated deploy, scan our code for live keys and tokens, and a match stops the deploy.

chunks.title: Security and data
chunks.heading: Security and data › What we confirm
chunks.text:
- We have no SOC 2 or ISO 27001 report and no third-party penetration test yet.
- Database backups are D1 Time Travel: we can restore the database to any minute in the last 30 days. Stored files (R2) have no versioning.
- Your data is stored in the United States: the database on Cloudflare D1 under its US jurisdiction, and files on Cloudflare R2 in Eastern North America.
- One person, the founder, has production access.
- A data processing agreement is available to Enterprise customers on request.
- No workspace feature calls an AI model: fixes, SDKs, docs and MCP servers are built by rules. The one model call is the site’s support chat, which sees only what you type into it.
- Vulnerability reports go to the address below.

## Subprocessors

| Subprocessor | What for | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cloudflare, Inc. | Hosting, content delivery and security; storage of orders, the dashboard, the CRM, sandbox sessions and Coati Pro data | United States, with a global network |
| Stripe | Card payments, fraud prevention and invoicing | United States and Ireland |
| Resend | Sending emails: download links, sign-in links, contact form messages | United States |
| GitHub, Inc. | Signing in to the workspace with GitHub, if you choose to (your GitHub id, login, name and verified email) | United States |
| Anthropic, PBC | Writing the support chat’s answers (the Claude API) | United States |
| Functional Software, Inc. (Sentry) | Error reports from our servers and our own pages, with identifiers removed first | United States |
| Better Stack, Inc. | Checking every few minutes that our public pages answer; it receives no personal data | United States |
